we present a practical method for in vivo estimation of the magnetization transfer macromolecular fraction, Mb0.
we have developed and tested a practical method for estimating the bound‐pool macroparticle fraction, Mb0, which is a true tissue‐specific MT parameter.

we present a practical method for in vivo estimation of the magnetization transfer macromolecular pool fraction, a true measure of the concentration of macromolecules in tissue, that can be used to estimate the concentration of macomolecules, and to compare magnetization transfer effects between studies.

the development of a practical method to obtain an in vivo estimate for the MT bound‐pool macomolecular fraction.
a practical method for estimating the MT bound‐pool fraction in vivo, which is an important parameter in understanding the MT effect and may prove useful in clinical studies.
the practical implementation of the MT bound‐pool fraction in the clinic and the development of a method that is simple, accurate, and robust.

the method is practical, and the results of the simulation are encouraging.
the proposed method allows a practical and accurate in vivo estimation of Mb0, a true tissue parameter that represents the semisolid concentration of protons involved in the MT effect.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method presented here is a low power method for estimating Mb0, which can be used in conjunction with MTR to provide a more comprehensive description of the MT effect.

we have developed a practical method for estimating Mb0, which allows the comparison of MT effects between different tissues and scanners, and which is useful for quantifying the MT effect of pathological tissue.
we present a method to estimate Mb0 in vivo using one saturation measurement, and that this method is feasible in expected tissue parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the low‐power MT method can be implemented in the clinic and is a useful tool for estimating tissue macromolecular fraction, which can be used in conjunction with other MRI methods for tissue characterization.

it is possible to estimate the bound‐pool fraction, Mb0, in vivo using low input power and a single measurement, thus allowing the use of this parameter as a biomarker of tissue damage in a clinical setting.

a low power, single measurement MT method can be used in the clinic to estimate Mb0, a true tissue parameter that can be used to compare the MT effect in different tissues or diseases, independent of input power and off‐resonant frequency.
